html:
SMTO-PRX-0011 — SMTO stopped waiting for Proxmox to finish

GUID: d45288b0-1095-4833-bb1c-734f9f63e1d6
Slug: proxmox-task-timeout
Domain: PRX · Subsystem: prx

What happened

  • Proxmox didn't finish the job within the time SMTO waits. The job may still be running on Proxmox or may already be done, so your change might have happened.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask the Agent to show the current status of the VM you were changing, without asking it to change anything. That tells you whether Proxmox already finished the job.
  2. If you can, open the Proxmox web interface and check the VM's Task History to see whether the task is still running. Slow jobs, such as a VM shutting down cleanly, can keep running after SMTO stops waiting.
  3. Only if the VM is not yet in the state you wanted and no task is still running, ask for the action again. Repeating a change that already happened or is still in progress can cause a second restart or stop.

What success looks like

  • The VM's status shows the state you wanted, and only one task for it appears in Proxmox's Task History.

If it still fails

  • Check whether the earlier action already happened before trying it again. Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages the Proxmox server. This was a wait on Proxmox, not on the AI model, so switching models won't help.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Proxmox operation deadline elapsed before the next API request or while polling a task UPID that was still running, so the remote task's outcome is unknown.

What this means

  • The shared operation deadline expires before another request or while waiting for the remote task to stop. Proxmox task and resource receipts own effect truth. A failed read, expired local wait or invalid response does not undo a mutation; diagnostics never replay writes or escalate graceful shutdown to forced stop.

Why this can happen

  • The shared operation deadline expires before another request or while waiting for the remote task to stop.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the original UPID and current guest/task state using supported observation.

How to fix it

  • The remote task may still be running. Read its status using the UPID in the error facts (or read current guest status) before repeating the mutation; the guest_power wait defaults to 120 seconds (timeout_seconds), and ending the local wait does not cancel the Proxmox task. This is a Proxmox wait, not a model timeout.
  • The remote task may still be running. Inspect its authoritative task status before repeating the mutation.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect and reconcile authoritative state before repeating any mutation or control request. Do not blindly retry.

How to verify the fix

  • The original remote outcome is known before any repeat mutation.

What not to do

  • Do not resubmit the same Proxmox mutation merely because waiting timed out.
  • Do not treat this as an LLM timeout.

Technical notes

  • Proxmox task and resource receipts own effect truth. A failed read, expired local wait or invalid response does not undo a mutation; diagnostics never replay writes or escalate graceful shutdown to forced stop.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.

Do not confuse with / related errors

  • SMTO-PRX-0005 — Proxmox mutation outcome is unknown
  • SMTO-EXE-0004 — Execution outcome is unknown
